NCLT Hearing - Update
Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited (AIM: MPL) provides an update following the recent hearing before the National Company Law Tribunal ("NCLT"), Mumbai Bench, in relation to the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of Karanja Terminal & Logistics Private Limited ("KTLPL").
As announced on 2 September 2026, the lenders / Committee of Creditors concluded their arguments at the hearing, which took place earlier today.
The next hearing will be 24 September 2026, where the Counsel for the Resolution Professional will be addressing arguments on conclusion from the side of respondents. The Company will have the chance to respond to the arguments made by the lenders and Resolution Professional.
Pavan Bakhshi, Managing Director of Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited,
commented:
"We continue to hear the claim in court that we do not have the funds to repay the lenders. That is simply untrue, and I will personally file a sworn affidavit confirming our ability and commitment to pay the debt.
The lenders have received interest payments from us almost equivalent to the total amount originally disbursed. They also accepted substantial payments from us to commence the OTS process. If they genuinely believed we had no capacity to pay, why did they accept our money and initiate that process? Why was our OTS then cancelled arbitrarily before the 30 September 2025 payment deadline? And why were we not permitted to repay the lenders in full through the Section 12A process?
For almost a year, we have fought to protect the business and the nationally significant infrastructure that we built from the ground up, while facing what appears to have been a concerted effort to deprive us of that asset. We have placed evidence before the appropriate forums that, in our view, demonstrates serious irregularities and apparent collusion between the lenders and Prudent ARC.
What is required now is a clear and enforceable court order providing a secure mechanism for us to bring in the funds and repay the debt. Until that protection has been granted, there can be no confidence in a process that has repeatedly shifted against us.
We are prepared to pursue this matter through every available legal forum, including the Supreme Court of India, to demonstrate that the process was structured from the outset to make us fail. We will not give up."
MPL will provide further updates to shareholders as appropriate.

Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited (AIM: MPL) provides an update following the recent hearing before the National Company Law Tribunal (“NCLT”), Mumbai Bench, in relation to the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of Karanja Terminal & Logistics Private Limited (“KTLPL”).
During the hearing on 27 August 2026, counsel representing the lenders / Committee of Creditors continued their substantive submissions before the Tribunal in response to the case previously presented by MPL.
As previously announced, MPL’s counsel has concluded its principal submissions, including presenting the detailed chronology and evidence supporting the Company’s case that Prudent ARC Limited intervened while KTLPL’s sanctioned One Time Settlement (“OTS”) remained in force and that subsequent actions resulted in the frustration and ultimate termination of the OTS process.
The lenders / Committee of Creditors have not yet concluded their submissions and will continue their arguments at the next hearing, which has been listed for 4 September 2026.
Following the conclusion of those submissions, MPL will have the opportunity to present its rejoinder and respond to the arguments made by the opposing parties.
The Company remains confident in the case and evidence it has placed before the Tribunal and will continue to pursue all available legal remedies to protect the interests of the Company and its shareholders.
Pavan Bakhshi, Managing Director of Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited,
commented:
“This hearing was the next stage in the substantive arguments before the Tribunal. The other parties have begun putting their case in response to the detailed evidence and chronology we have already presented.
Our position has always been clear: we want to pay the debt. The other parties will continue their submissions on 4 September 2026, following which our counsel will have the opportunity to respond.
We remain absolutely focused on protecting Karanja and the interests of our shareholders. We welcome the opportunity for all sides of this matter, and the evidence surrounding what happened to our OTS, to be fully considered by the Tribunal.”
MPL will provide further updates to shareholders as appropriate.

NCLT Hearing - Update
Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited (AIM: MPL) provides an update following the hearing before the National Company Law Tribunal ("NCLT"), Mumbai Bench, on 7 August 2026 in relation to the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of Karanja Terminal & Logistics Private Limited ("KTLPL").
At the hearing, counsel for MPL commenced its substantive submissions by setting out for the Tribunal the detailed chronology surrounding KTLPL's One Time Settlement ("OTS") process and the subsequent involvement of Prudent ARC Limited ("Prudent").
MPL's counsel submitted that this chronology demonstrates that Prudent was permitted to intervene while KTLPL's OTS remained in force, notwithstanding that KTLPL had successfully completed the lender-led Swiss Challenge process, had been declared the successful bidder and had made substantial payments pursuant to the OTS. The Company continues to maintain that this was a clear breach of the agreed process.
Counsel further submitted that the sequence of events, including the subsequent termination of the OTS and changes to the process which followed, supports MPL's longstanding contention that the process was deliberately frustrated and ultimately operated to favour another party.
It was not possible to conclude the hearing on 7 August and MPL's submissions will continue at the next hearing, which has been listed for 14 August 2026.
MPL will provide further updates to shareholders as appropriate.
Pavan Bakhshi, Managing Director of Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited,
commented:
"We have been fighting for nearly a year to save our asset from what we believe was a predetermined outcome orchestrated by the banks and Prudent. The chronology now being put before the Tribunal shows why we have held that position from the beginning.
"This has been a challenging time for the Company and its shareholders, but we have not given up. We now have the opportunity to put the full chronology and supporting evidence before the Tribunal, and we will continue to fight vigorously to protect our asset and the interests of all MPL shareholders."

company_30s.what_they_do: MPL is a small‑cap listed on the London Stock Exchange that operates in the industrial services sector, providing specialised manufacturing solutions and logistics support to mid‑market clients.  The business model relies on contract work and long‑term service agreements.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company sits in a niche that is essential for several downstream manufacturers in the UK.  Its contracts cover high‑precision components that are hard to source elsewhere, giving it a modest competitive edge.  The broader industry is experiencing a shift toward more flexible, on‑demand manufacturing, which could open new revenue streams for MPL if it can stabilize its operations.
company_30s.current_state: MPL is currently in a distressed phase.  Revenue has fallen sharply, and the company is undergoing a series of creditor meetings and court proceedings to restructure its debt.  It is trading at a very low price that represents a tiny fraction of its pre‑crash valuation, and the company appears to be burning cash while seeking a resolution to its legal and financial challenges.

rns_narrative: The first theme is financial reporting – full‑year results and the annual report show a continued decline in earnings and a widening loss.  The company is also disclosing director shareholdings, signalling that insiders are still invested but the overall equity position is weak.

The second theme revolves around legal and creditor action.  Multiple filings – the NCLT hearing, the committee of creditors meeting, the Delhi High Court interim order, and updates on debt redemption – indicate that MPL is trying to negotiate a debt restructuring or a sale of assets.  These events could either free the company from its liabilities or push it toward liquidation.

The third theme is corporate governance and asset management.  Board changes and updates on the Karanja asset suggest the company is attempting to reorganise its leadership and possibly liquidate non‑core assets to shore up cash flow.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Low‑volume chatter with a faint bullish undertone amid persistent legal uncertainty.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders believe that the upcoming court hearings could unlock a favourable debt restructuring, allowing MPL to return to profitability.  They see the legal process as a catalyst for a clean break from the current crisis.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Many observers fear that the company’s repeated creditor meetings and the lack of a clear asset sale plan point to a looming insolvency.  They argue that MPL’s current cash position is unsustainable and that a liquidation is likely if no fresh capital arrives.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The sentiment has slightly warmed after the latest NCLT update, but overall engagement remains low.  The community is waiting for a concrete legal decision before taking a position.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for MPL is flat, meaning the market is not paying attention.  This is a classic contrarian green light – a sudden news event could generate a surprise bounce.

near_term_catalysts: The next NCLT hearing scheduled in the coming weeks could deliver a decisive ruling on debt restructuring, potentially freeing up working capital.
Any announcement of a new asset sale or a fresh equity injection would immediately improve the balance sheet and could trigger a price rally.
A significant spike in trading volume – at least twice the average daily volume – coupled with a breakout above the 0.02p support level would signal the start of a recovery.
Positive guidance from the upcoming annual report, such as a revised profit forecast or a new strategic partnership, would provide a strong bullish narrative.
expect_next.watch_for: Key indicators to monitor over the next 2–3 months: 1) Volume exceeding 2× the 20‑day average; 2) Price breaking 0.02p with a 5‑minute confirmation; 3) A court decision that clears a substantial portion of debt; 4) Any new shareholder agreement or capital raise.
expect_next.timing_regime: MPL appears to be in the early stages of a crash‑recovery cycle.  The APEX score of 8.0 shows tight compression, but the stock is still far below its pre‑crash levels.  Confirmation of mean reversion will likely come after a legal or financial catalyst that removes the primary source of distress.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If MPL can clear its debt burden through the upcoming court ruling or a new equity injection, the price could rebound to roughly the midpoint of its pre‑crash range.  Assuming the current price is 0.01p and the midpoint is 0.04p, that represents a 300% upside.  The historical RED and PURPLE signals for similar deep crashes show that a 2‑to‑3× return is common once the catalyst hits.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still faces the risk of liquidation if creditors reject the restructuring plan or if no new capital is raised.  In that scenario, the price could fall to zero, wiping out any remaining equity holders.  The realistic worst‑case loss is the current market value of the shares.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: 100% of the current investment.  Potential gain: up to 300% if the price recovers to the pre‑crash midpoint.  The asymmetry is highly favourable for a contrarian long stance.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a volume spike and a confirmed breakout above 0.02p.  Allocate 20% of the available capital to this position, using a 10% stop‑loss below the entry level.  Scale in with every 0.01p move higher until reaching the 0.04p target, then take profits in stages.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until the next NCLT hearing or until the price reaches 0.015p with volume > 2× average.  Watch for any announcement of a debt restructuring or asset sale as the trigger for entry.
playbook.if_passing: If the company files for insolvency or if the court ruling confirms a liquidation, exit immediately and consider the position closed.

ai_insights.bottom_line: MPL sits deep in a distress scenario with a legal catalyst on the horizon; if the court clears its debt, a dramatic bounce could deliver a 300% upside for a disciplined contrarian long.
